purposeAndApplication.purpose: The Brother DA-927A is a Japan-manufactured, narrow cylinder-bed, feed-off-the-arm industrial double chain stitch sewing machine. It is classified under ISO stitch type 401 (double chain stitch) and is engineered for high-volume garment manufacturing operations where tubular workpieces — such as trouser legs, jeans inseams, and sleeves — cannot be accommodated on a standard flat-bed machine.

title: Brother DA-927A
subtitle: Twin/Three Needle Feed Off-the-Arm Double Chain Stitcher
overviewDescription: The Brother DA-927A is a Japan-manufactured, narrow cylinder-bed, feed-off-the-arm industrial double chain stitch sewing machine produced by Brother Industries, Ltd. It is classified under ISO stitch type 401 (double chain stitch) and is engineered for high-volume garment manufacturing operations where tubular workpieces — such as trouser legs, jeans inseams, and sleeves — cannot be accommodated on a standard flat-bed machine. Three material-weight variants exist under the DA-927A designation: -1 for light materials (shirts, underwear), -2 for light-to-medium materials (blended fabrics, sportswear), and -3 for medium-weight materials (denim, work-wear). The related DA-928A extends the series to heavy (-5) and extra-heavy/denim (-7) applications using three needles. The double chain stitch offers approximately 30% greater seam elasticity compared to ISO 301 lockstitch, which is critical for stretch fabrics and garments subject to repeated flexion during wear. Because no bobbin is used, the machine can run continuously without interruption for bobbin replacement, significantly increasing production throughput.

workingPrinciples.heading: 1. Chain Stitch Formation (ISO 401)
workingPrinciples.description: The DA-927A produces a double chain stitch (stitch type 401) using two independent thread systems: upper needle thread(s) and lower looper thread(s). No bobbin is used. Stitch formation proceeds through the following five-phase cycle: 1) Needle descent: The upper shaft cam drives the needle bar connecting rod, pushing the needle(s) through the fabric. The needle carries a loop of upper thread below the needle plate level. 2) Loop capture: As the needle begins to rise, a slack loop forms on the back of the needle. The looper, driven by the eccentric wheel on the lower shaft, swings forward and enters this loop, capturing the upper thread. 3) Loop expansion: The looper moves forward (away from the needle), spreading the captured upper thread loop wide enough for the needle to pass through it on the next downstroke. 4) Interlock: On the next needle descent, the needle(s) pass through the open loop of the looper thread, linking consecutive upper thread loops through the looper thread to form the chain on the underside of the fabric. 5) Loop tightening and feeding: The thread take-up levers (upper and lower) pull excess thread back, tightening the stitch node at the midpoint of the fabric layers. The feed dogs simultaneously advance the fabric by one stitch length.

workingPrinciples.heading: 2. Feed-Off-the-Arm Mechanism
workingPrinciples.description: The fabric feeds horizontally around the narrow cylinder arm rather than across a flat bed. The main feed dog and sub-feed dog (forward feed arm) work in differential mode to prevent puckering or stretching of the seam. The eccentric wheel assembly on the lower shaft translates rotary motion into the elliptical feed dog stroke (rise, advance, drop, return).

workingPrinciples.heading: 3. Minimum Lubrication System
workingPrinciples.description: The DA-927A departs from full-oil predecessors by supplying lubricant only to the needle bar and upper shaft via felt wicks (wick holder SB7805001; wick 3×3 SB7806001; wick 2×2 SB7811001). All lower mechanisms run dry. This prevents oil migration onto light or white fabric surfaces, a critical quality requirement in modern garment production.

sequenceFlow.stepDescription: Thread upper needle threads through guides and tension discs
Thread lower looper threads through looper threading path
Adjust needle guard position for proper clearance
Knee-lift presser; place workpiece in cylinder arm
Release knee lifter; depress treadle to start

sequenceFlow.stepTitle: Move to chain trimmer; blank stitch
sequenceFlow.stepDescription: Move to chain trimmer; blank stitch for chain off
Cut chain thread using chaining-off knife; remove workpiece
End-of-shift: lint removal and machine cleaning
Needle guard re-check after stitch length change

partsList.function: Outer protective cover on the front face of the machine head. Shields internal mechanisms and provides the exterior surface for the machine.
Gasket/seal between the face plate and the machine body. Prevents oil from seeping out through the face plate joint.
Protective guard that covers the oscillating thread take-up lever to protect operator from moving parts and reduce thread snagging.
Cap that closes the end of the forward feed arm cover, sealing the interior of the arm mechanism from dust and lint.
Sealing gasket fitted between the front feed arm cap and the arm body. Maintains a dust and oil-tight seal.
Cover plate protecting the ball bearing housing on the upper shaft end from contamination.
Gasket seated between the ball bearing cover and the machine frame. Prevents lubricant leakage around the bearing housing.
Main hinged front access cover of the machine body. Allows operator access to the feed and looper mechanisms for threading and adjustment.
Return springs that keep the front cover in the closed position during sewing and allow it to snap open when released for servicing.
Latching hooks that secure the front cover in the closed position, preventing unintended opening during operation.
Pivot hinges on which the front cover swings open. Must be correctly aligned to ensure the cover seals fully when closed.
Blanking plugs sealing unused access holes in the machine body to prevent ingress of lint and foreign material.
Left-side hinge assembly for the looper guide cover. Enables the cover to be opened for looper access and threading.
Right-side hinge assembly for the looper guide cover. Works in tandem with the left hinge to support the cover panel.
Retention springs that hold the looper side cover in the closed and secured position during sewing operations.
Transparent sight-glass window fitted into the machine body through which the operator monitors the lubricating oil level. Two positions allow viewing from either side.
Large-diameter retention screws used to secure structural machine body panels.
Oil-resistant rubber O-rings sealing the screw plugs in the oil tank/body to prevent oil leakage around the fastener threads.
Blanking plug for the main oil fill port, removed when adding lubricating oil to the reservoir.
Small blanking plug for auxiliary oil port or access hole on the machine body.
General purpose rubber blanking cap used on the machine body for various port sealing applications.
Large-diameter blanking plug covering the main shaft access port on the machine head casting.
Vibration-damping rubber cushions placed between the machine head and the mounting table to absorb motor and mechanism vibration.
Collar spacers maintaining the correct standoff distance between the machine body and the table mounting bracket.
Mounting plates that interface the machine base with the table. Provides the correct positional reference for the machine on the sewing table.
Rubber isolation elements fitted around the table mounting bolts to absorb vibration and prevent surface damage to the table.
Spacer collars fitted on the table mounting fasteners to maintain correct clamping geometry.
Plain washers distributing clamping load evenly across the mounting bracket surfaces.
Right/rear side cover for the looper compartment (927A-specific). Seals the looper area from lint and provides a guard for the looper movement.
Left-side looper compartment cover (927A-specific). Completes the enclosure of the looper mechanism.
Spring roll pin securing the looper cover hinge or retention feature. Provides locking force through its elastic tension.
Complete handwheel assembly mounted on the right side of the machine. Used by the operator to manually rotate the upper shaft for needle positioning, threading, and timing checks.
Toothed timing pulleys mounted on the upper and lower shafts. Work in conjunction with the timing belt to synchronise the upper shaft, needle bar, and lower shaft looper mechanism at a 1:1 ratio.
Precision spacers maintaining the correct axial positioning of the timing pulleys on their respective shafts.

Toothed synchronous drive belt linking the upper shaft timing pulley to the lower shaft timing pulley. Maintains exact 1:1 phase relationship between needle and looper, essential for stitch formation.
Protective guard enclosing the timing belt and pulleys on the rear side of the machine. Prevents operator contact and protects the belt from lint contamination.
Secondary cover plate completing the enclosure of the belt/pulley area. Removable for timing belt inspection and replacement.
Additional small cover panel in the pulley mechanism area providing access protection.
Spring-loaded idler pulley assembly that maintains correct tension on the timing belt throughout the operating speed range.
Radial ball bearings supporting the tension pulley on its shaft. Enables smooth, low-friction rotation of the idler pulley.
Circlip retaining rings that axially lock the ball bearings within the tension pulley bore.
Collar providing the correct width spacing for the tension pulley bearing assembly on its mounting bolt.
Bracket on which the tension pulley assembly is mounted. Allows positional adjustment to set correct timing belt tension.
Base bracket to which the pulley cover panels (A and B) are attached. Forms the structural foundation of the pulley guard assembly.
Front section of the two-piece pulley cover. Shields the handwheel drive pulley from accidental contact and lint ingress.
Rear section of the pulley cover, completing the enclosure. Must be correctly seated to ensure the handwheel rotates freely inside the guard.
Precision shoulder screws used as pivots or positional fasteners in the pulley cover assembly. Their machined shoulder provides an exact positional reference.
Foam or felt sheet inserts lining the interior of the pulley cover. Reduces vibration noise and prevents the cover from rattling against the pulley.
Complete upper shaft assembly including shaft, bearings, and timing pulley. The primary power transmission shaft converting motor rotation into needle bar reciprocating motion via the connecting rod.
Machined steel main shaft running horizontally through the machine head. Carries the thread take-up crank and needle bar connecting rod eccentric. Rotates at machine speed (up to 4,000 rpm).
Precision thrust ball bearings supporting the upper shaft at each end. Absorbs axial and radial loads generated during high-speed operation.
External circlip locking the bearing on the upper shaft against axial displacement.
Internal circlip retaining the bearing within the housing bore.
Precision-machined housing holding the upper shaft bearing in correct alignment with the machine head casting.
Additional deep-groove ball bearing supporting an intermediate point of the upper shaft. The NR suffix indicates an integral snap ring groove for positional retention.
Companion deep-groove ball bearing providing radial support to the upper shaft at the second journal position.
Eccentric crank assembly mounted on the upper shaft (927A variant, medium-high lift). Converts upper shaft rotation into the oscillating motion of the upper thread take-up lever.
The machined eccentric crank component within the above assembly. The offset determines the stroke and timing of the thread take-up.
Higher-lift thread take-up crank assembly for the DA-928A heavy-duty variant, providing a larger take-up stroke suitable for heavier thread.
Machined eccentric crank (high lift version) within the 928A take-up assy.
Connecting rod assembly linking the upper shaft eccentric to the needle bar clamp. Converts the rotary motion of the upper shaft into the linear 30 mm reciprocating stroke of the needle bar.
Clamp that attaches the bottom end of the needle bar connecting rod to the needle bar, transmitting the connecting rod's reciprocating motion directly to the needle bar.
Pin/shaft forming the pivot joint between the connecting rod and the needle bar clamp, allowing the angular change between connecting rod and needle bar to be accommodated.
Precision-fitted rectangular block that slides within the needle bar guide channel, constraining the needle bar to strictly vertical (linear) motion and preventing any lateral deviation.
Fixed vertical guide channel machined into or attached to the machine head frame. The guide slide block runs inside this channel, defining the straight vertical path of the needle bar.
The main vertical reciprocating rod that holds the needle clamp at its lower end. Moves up and down 30 mm with each stitch cycle, driving the needle through the fabric.
Upper bronze or self-lubricating bush providing precise bearing support to the needle bar at the top of its travel. Maintains needle bar alignment and absorbs side loads.
Lower bush supporting the needle bar at the bottom of the guide. Together with the upper bush, ensures the needle remains perfectly vertical throughout its stroke.
Oil feed tube assembly delivering lubricating oil from the felt wick system to the needle bar. Part of the minimum lubrication system for the upper mechanism.
Mounting bracket holding the oil-absorbing felt pad in position against the needle bar. Regulates the rate of oil delivery to the needle bar surface.

Holder locating the oil-wicking felt cords (Wick 3×3 and Wick 2×2) in position to absorb oil from the reservoir and deliver it by capillary action to lubrication points on the upper shaft and needle bar.
Braided felt wick cord (3 mm × 3 mm cross-section) providing capillary oil transport from the oil reservoir to the upper shaft bearing area as part of the minimum lubrication system.
Smaller braided felt wick cord (2 mm × 2 mm) delivering capillary oil to the needle bar bush or presser bar bush lubrication point. Used in both Section C and Section D.

Vertical rod carrying the presser foot at its lower end. Applies downward spring pressure to hold fabric against the needle plate during stitching. The 927A variant is matched to light-to-medium fabric weight.
Heavier-duty presser bar for the DA-928A variant, dimensioned for the higher clamping loads required for heavy and denim materials.
Screw located at the top of the presser bar spring assembly. Turning this screw compresses or releases the presser bar spring, adjusting foot pressure between 39.2 N (4 kgf) and 78.4 N (8 kgf).
Bronze or sintered bearing bush providing a close-fit sliding support for the presser bar within the machine head casting. Ensures the bar moves vertically without lateral play.
Bracket that aligns and guides the lower section of the presser bar, preventing rotation of the bar and maintaining the presser foot in the correct orientation relative to the needle plate slots.
Coil compression spring acting on the presser bar to apply downward force to the presser foot. The spring constant is matched to the 927A's light/medium material applications.
Higher-rate coil spring for the 928A heavy-duty variant, providing greater presser foot pressure appropriate for thick denim and heavy materials.
Guide tube or collar that locates and constrains the presser bar spring concentrically around the presser bar, preventing buckling and ensuring uniform spring force delivery.
Plain washer distributing the spring load across the presser bar adjusting screw seat to prevent damage to the screw tip and spring end.
Cam lever that, when operated by the knee lifter lever, raises the presser bar (and foot) against the spring force to allow insertion or removal of the workpiece.
Precision shoulder screw forming the pivot pin on which the presser bar lifter rotates within the machine head.

The lever arm connected by chain to the knee lift pedal below the table. When the operator presses the pedal with their knee, this lever actuates the presser bar lifter to raise the presser foot up to 10 mm.
Pivot screw for the knee lifter lever, providing a precision bearing surface for the lever rotation.
Torsion return spring that returns the knee lifter lever to its rest position after the knee pedal is released, ensuring the presser foot applies full spring pressure when released.

Complete eccentric wheel assembly for the DA-927A series. The eccentric (offset) mounting converts the lower shaft's rotary motion into the elliptical feed stroke of the feed dog (rise → advance → drop → return).
Eccentric wheel assembly variant for the DA-928A. Different eccentric radius compared to 927A to suit the heavier material feed requirements.
Spring roll pins locking eccentric components on the lower shaft or feed mechanism shafts. Their split construction provides clamping force to resist rotation on the shaft.
Torsion spring providing the return force in the stitch length ratchet-stop mechanism, holding the eccentric wheel at the set stitch length position against vibration.
Small screw anchoring the ratchet return spring to its mounting location.
Precision sleeve providing the bearing surface between the eccentric wheel and the lower shaft or feed bar, ensuring smooth eccentric rotation without shaft wear.
Eccentric wheel fitted with integral locking screw for the DA-927A medium-speed variant. The lock screw secures the wheel at the correct stitch length setting on the shaft.
Higher-throw eccentric wheel for the DA-928A, providing greater feed dog stroke appropriate for heavy material. Fitted with integral lock screw.
Slide block assembly that converts the eccentric wheel's rotary-eccentric motion into the linear reciprocating motion of the feed bar. Guides the feed stroke horizontally along the arm axis.
Vertical connecting rod linking the feed bar slide block to the feed dog, transmitting the vertical (rise/drop) component of the elliptical feed stroke to the feed dog teeth.
Shaft on which the vertical feed connecting rod pivots. Provides the precise geometric relationship between the eccentric motion and the feed dog vertical movement.
The eccentric shaft element within the feed bar assembly, providing the phase offset that produces the combined vertical and horizontal feed dog motion (elliptical path).
Oil-resistant rubber O-ring sealing the feed bar eccentric shaft bore to prevent lubricant leakage into the feed mechanism.

The stitch length adjustment push button accessed from the side of the machine. Pressing this button releases the eccentric wheel from its locked position, allowing the operator to rotate the eccentric and set a new stitch length.
Return spring that pushes the stitch length push button back out to the rest (locked) position after adjustment, re-engaging the stitch length lock.
Sealing O-ring around the push button shaft, preventing oil leakage through the button aperture.
Small plain washer at the push button shaft end, distributing load and providing a seating surface for the retaining ring.
External E-type retaining ring locking the stitch length push button assembly in position on its shaft.
Complete twin-needle clamp assembly. Holds two Organ TV×64NY needles at the correct gauge spacing and ensures the long groove of each needle faces front for proper thread loop formation.
Three-needle clamp assembly for 1/8 in × 2-1 gauge. Holds three needles at 1/8 in spacing for three-needle double chain stitch applications.
Organ TV×64NY industrial chain stitch needle in size #12 for light material variant (927A-1). The long groove guides upper thread into the needle eye without friction damage.
Size #14 needle for light-to-medium material variant (927A-2). Larger shaft and eye accommodate heavier thread used on medium weight fabrics.
Size #16 needle for medium material variant (927A-3). Largest needle in the 927A series, for denim and work-wear applications.

Throat plate mounted on top of the cylinder bed. Contains calibrated slots through which the feed dog teeth project and needle hole(s) through which the needle passes. The underside guides the fabric over the cylinder bed surface.

Complete presser foot assembly for the 927A gauge. The foot bears against the top surface of the fabric, applying the clamping pressure set by the adjusting screw. The foot geometry matches the needle plate slots and feed dog position.
Retention pins securing the presser foot sections or spring elements within the foot assembly.
The main spring element within the presser foot assembly that distributes even pressure across the foot width, preventing uneven material feeding or puckering.
Safety guard plate mounted near the needle(s) to deflect the operator's fingers away from the needle impact zone. Mandatory safety device that must always be in place during operation.

Toothed feed plate that rises through the needle plate slots and advances the fabric by one stitch length per cycle. The tooth geometry and row spacing are matched to the material type and stitch length range.
Bracket that mounts the needle guard in the correct positional relationship to the looper tip and needle. Must be readjusted every time the stitch length is changed.

The actual deflector blade of the needle guard for the twin-needle 927A. Prevents the needle from flexing laterally into the path of the advancing looper tip, avoiding broken loopers and skipped stitches.
Three-needle variant needle guard, shaped to protect all three needles simultaneously in the 1/8×2-1 gauge configuration.
Flat guide plate inserted through the forward feed arm cap slot when the optional lapper is fitted. Directs the fabric edge to the lapper fold point for flat-fell or lap seam production.
Washer providing the correct clearance between the lapper guide plate and its mounting slot to permit smooth forward sliding of the guide plate.

Complete lapper folder attachment used for flat-fell seam construction on shirts, jeans, and similar garments. Folds and guides the fabric edge under the seam allowance for a neat enclosed seam finish.

The large (left-side) looper of the twin or three-needle configuration. Catches the upper thread loop from the left needle and interlocks it with the lower looper thread to form the chain on the fabric underside.
The small (right-side) looper of the twin-needle configuration. Catches the upper thread loop from the right needle, forming the right-side chain stitch.
Middle looper for the three-needle configuration. Catches the loop from the centre needle, producing the middle stitch row of a three-needle chain seam.
Bracket mounting the large (L) looper to the looper shaft link. Positions the looper tip at the precise geometric relationship to the needle for correct loop capture timing.
Bracket mounting the small (S) looper, maintaining its precise position relative to the right needle for stitch formation.
Bracket mounting the middle looper for three-needle operation.

Complete lower shaft assembly. The lower shaft runs horizontally through the cylinder arm, driven at a 1:1 ratio from the upper shaft via the timing belt. Carries the eccentric wheel for looper actuation and the feed eccentric for feed dog motion.
The precision-ground steel shaft itself. Rotates in synchrony with the upper shaft, ensuring the looper tip arrives at the needle at the exact moment the needle loop is at its maximum size.

Thrust ball bearing supporting the lower shaft within the cylinder arm. Identical specification to the upper shaft bearing, ensuring consistent support under the loads generated by the looper and feed mechanisms.
Additional radial ball bearing supporting an intermediate journal of the lower shaft within the arm. Prevents shaft deflection under operating loads.
Second additional radial ball bearing at the outboard end of the lower shaft, completing the three-point support of the lower shaft within the cylinder arm.
A journal bearing bush supplementing the ball bearings at a lubrication-point position on the lower shaft, accommodating minor shaft flexure during high-speed operation.

Eccentric wheel mounted on the lower shaft that drives the looper motion. The offset (eccentricity) determines the stroke of the looper forward-backward movement. The integral screw locks it to the lower shaft at the timing position.
928A-specific eccentric wheel, with different eccentricity to produce the higher looper stroke needed for the heavier 928A stitch configuration.

Sleeve bearing between the eccentric wheel and the connecting rod eye, allowing smooth relative rotation and converting the eccentric's circular motion into the oscillating stroke of the looper connecting rod.

A forked link that converts one plane of the connecting rod's motion into the looper's rocking (side-to-side) movement. The fork allows the looper to rock transversally while the connecting rod operates in the fore-aft plane.
Pivot shaft on which the looper feeding fork rocks. Precisely located relative to the lower shaft axis to define the geometry of the looper's rocking path.
Bracket clamped to the lower shaft that holds the looper feeding fork shaft. Its angular position on the lower shaft is critical: it determines the timing and extent of the looper's rocking motion.
Connecting rod linking the eccentric wheel to the looper shaft link. Translates the eccentric wheel's rotation into the reciprocating (forward-backward) motion of the looper.
Shaft on which the looper connecting rod pivots at its upper end, providing the rotational degree of freedom needed to accommodate the connecting rod's changing angle during operation.
A guide plate constraining the looper connecting rod to its correct plane of motion, preventing torsional twisting that could alter looper timing.

Complete link set connecting the looper connecting rod motion to the looper shaft, transmitting both the forward-backward and rocking motions to the looper. The geometry of this link set determines the shape of the looper's path.
Front journal bearing supporting the looper shaft as it exits the front of the cylinder arm. Provides smooth low-friction support for the looper shaft's combined oscillating and rocking motion.
Rear journal bearing supporting the looper shaft at the back end of its bearing run. Works with the front bush to maintain the looper shaft in precise alignment.

The main shaft to which the looper holders (and thus the loopers themselves) are clamped. Carries out the combined forward-backward translation and rocking motion that produces the looper's tip path — the path that enters and expands the upper thread loop.
First guide in the upper threading path. Routes the needle thread(s) from the cotton stand into the machine's tension and take-up system along the correct path to avoid friction or tangling.
Secondary thread routing guide on the machine arm, directing thread toward the tension bracket at the correct angle.
Mounting bracket that carries all the upper thread tension components (tension studs, discs, springs, and nuts) for both needles in a compact, accessible assembly on the front face of the machine.

Complete pre-assembled upper thread tension unit for the DA-927A twin-needle configuration, including tension studs, discs, felts, springs, washers, and nuts. Controls needle thread tension for both needle threads simultaneously.
Three-needle version of the upper thread tension assembly for DA-927A. Controls thread tension for all three needle threads.
Individual tension adjustment springs within the tension assembly. One spring per needle thread provides independent fine-tune capability for thread tension balance between needles.
Threaded stud on which the tension disc stack is assembled. One stud per needle thread; the disc stack is clamped on each stud to apply friction-based tension to the thread.
Small thread eyelet guide mounted near each tension stud, keeping the thread centred between the tension discs as it passes through.
Felt washers within the tension disc stack that provide a consistent, non-abrasive friction surface between the steel discs and the thread. Prevents thread damage from metal-on-thread contact.

Polished steel discs (two per thread path) forming the main friction members of the thread tension assembly. Thread passes between each pair of discs; the clamping force of the tension nut determines the tension applied.
Knurled nut tightened by the operator to compress the tension disc stack, increasing thread tension. Loosening reduces tension.
Cap or presser plate at the outer end of each tension stud that retains the disc stack while allowing the tension nut to compress the assembly.

Pin linked to the tension release mechanism. When the presser foot is raised, the release pin automatically opens the tension discs, releasing thread tension and allowing thread to run freely for easy re-threading.

Shaft running across the tension bracket that transmits the presser bar lift motion to all tension release pins simultaneously, ensuring all needle thread tensions are released at once when the presser foot is raised.
Crank arm fixed to the tension release shaft. Converts the rotary motion of the release shaft into the linear displacement of the tension release pins.
Lever actuated by the presser bar lift mechanism that rotates the tension release shaft when the presser foot is raised, triggering simultaneous tension release on all needles.

Complete oscillating thread take-up assembly including the lever, holder, and spring. The take-up oscillates in synchrony with the needle bar: it rises as the needle rises (pulling thread up to tighten the loop) and descends as the needle descends (feeding thread down into the new loop).
The oscillating lever arm itself. Driven by the take-up crank on the upper shaft. The eye at the lever tip through which thread passes moves up and down approximately 28–35 mm per cycle.

A small thread-retaining clip or guide mounted on the take-up lever that holds the thread in the lever eye during the descent phase, preventing the thread from jumping out of the guide under high-speed running.
Mounting bracket on which the thread take-up lever assembly is pivoted, locating it at the correct geometric position relative to the upper shaft crank for proper take-up stroke.
Fixed thread guide positioned above the take-up lever eye. Routes the thread into the lever at the correct angle and prevents excessive thread ballooning during high-speed operation.
Lower fixed guide on the threading path below the take-up lever, routing thread smoothly into the needle bar area without sharp bends.
Washer behind the upper thread guide ensuring the guide sits flat against the machine face and the thread entry angle is correct.

Spring-loaded retainer clip at each tension stud position that holds the thread in the tension disc stack while the machine is being threaded. Prevents thread from slipping out of the discs before the machine starts.
Plate mounting multiple thread guides in a single assembly for three-needle configurations, keeping all three thread paths parallel and correctly spaced into the tension bracket.
The primary guide bracket at the top of the lower (looper) threading path. Routes the looper thread from the thread stand into the machine's lower threading system at the correct angle and position.
Secondary support bracket for the lower thread path, keeping the thread guide retainer correctly oriented and preventing vibration-induced misalignment.
Mounting bracket carrying all lower thread tension components. The looper thread tension is set independently of the needle thread tension via this bracket's tension assembly.
Fixed guide on the lower threading path below the tension bracket, routing looper thread from the tension assembly toward the lower take-up lever.
Fixed thread guide on the inner face of the cylinder arm routing the looper thread(s) through the arm interior toward the looper area. Prevents thread from snagging on the arm mechanism.

Complete lower thread take-up assembly bracket. The lower take-up works in opposition to the upper take-up: it pulls looper thread up on the descent (feeding thread into the new loop) and releases it on the rise (tightening the chain).
Cover plate protecting the lower thread take-up lever from lint and thread tangles, while still allowing the operator to observe lever operation.
Bracket mounting the lower thread take-up lever on the cylinder arm. Positional adjustment of this bracket changes the lower thread take-up timing and loop size.
Base bracket for the lower thread take-up system, providing the positional reference for the entire lower take-up assembly on the arm.
Thread guide at the output of the lower take-up assembly, routing the looper thread from the take-up lever into the lower arm area.
Thread guide associated with the lower take-up loop control, directing thread at the precise angle into the take-up lever to ensure consistent loop sizes in the underside chain.
Additional fixed guide within the lower threading mechanism that supports even thread flow into the lower take-up lever.
Base component of the lower thread release mechanism. Provides the mounting for the lower thread presser that opens lower thread tension when the presser foot is raised.
The moving element of the lower thread release mechanism. Engages the lower thread tension disc stack and opens the discs when the tension release shaft is actuated (presser foot raised).
Flat guide plate routing the looper thread along the inner face of the cylinder arm from the lower take-up area toward the looper thread guide bracket.

The lower thread take-up lever with screw for the DA-927A. This lever oscillates vertically (927A standard: 7 mm above take-up base at reference position) to meter looper thread into each stitch loop.
Higher-stroke lower thread take-up for DA-928A, adjusted to 5 mm above the take-up base reference position (different from 927A).
Guide bracket in the cylinder arm that constrains the lower thread along the feed direction, preventing thread oscillation at high speed.
Bracket at the tip of the cylinder arm mounting the final looper thread guide before the looper itself. Positions the thread guide at the correct angle for thread to enter the looper eye.

Complete lower thread tension disc assembly including felt discs, steel discs, and tension nut. Sets the looper thread tension to balance correctly with the needle thread tension for uniform stitch formation.
Mounting base for the lower thread guide assembly, fixing the thread path geometry at the cylinder arm tip.
General-purpose thread guide used at multiple positions in the lower threading path to maintain correct thread routing and prevent thread chafing on metal edges.
Plain washer used to shim or seat various lower thread guide components to achieve correct threading height.
Right-side hinge plate for mounting accessories or guards on the machine. Provides a pivot point for removable attachments such as thread guides or lapper components.
Left-side hinge plate counterpart to the right hinge plate, completing the hinge pair for accessory mounting on both sides of the machine.
Precision hinge pins forming the pivot axis for the hinge plates, allowing accessories to swing open for access and close for operation.
Bracket that holds the thread guide bar on the machine body, providing the mounting point for thread stand components.

The complete thread stand assembly consisting of the vertical support rod, thread spool pins, and thread guide fingers. Holds the spools of upper and lower thread above the machine at the correct height for unwinding without nesting.
Support bracket that fixes the thread stand to the machine table or machine body. Prevents the thread stand from swaying or rotating during high-speed operation.
Horizontal crossbar at the top of the thread stand from which the individual thread guide wires or rods are suspended to each spool position.
Small guide eyelets at the end of each thread guide wire, positioned directly above each spool to centre the thread as it unwinds, preventing the thread from falling off the spool edge.
Flexible or semi-rigid wire guides routing thread from each spool to the machine's front tension bracket. Individual wires prevent thread crossover between adjacent spools.
Detachable pins inserted into the thread stand crossbar on which the thread spools are placed. Must be removed to change spools and reinserted to hold the spool in position during sewing.
Cap or knob at the outer end of the thread spool pin, preventing the spool from sliding off the pin during operation.
Main support shaft of the thread stand, running vertically from the table mounting to the thread guide bar. The primary structural column of the thread stand assembly.
Spring-loaded or friction retainer that holds the thread spool on its pin, preventing the spool from spinning freely and unravelling when the machine stops.
Rubber dampers or cushions at the thread stand mounting points that absorb vibration from the machine and prevent it from transmitting into the thread stand.
Plain washers used at the thread stand mounting joints to distribute clamping loads and achieve the correct seat height for the thread guide bar.
Standard M6 socket or hex head screws used to secure thread stand components to the machine table or mounting bracket.
Anodised aluminium or stainless steel tension plates used as anti-friction surfaces at thread guide positions. Prevents thread from chafing against the machine body at high-speed.
Cylinder-arm-mounted thread guide for the lower thread path, routing looper thread along the inside face of the cylinder arm toward the looper.
Small locating pins that retain the arm thread guide in its correct position within the cylinder arm bore.
Thin washers used as shims behind the arm thread guide to adjust its depth position within the arm bore.
Felt discs placed under the thread spool on its pin to dampen spool vibration and prevent the spool from rattling against the spool pin during operation.

Large-diameter thread spool caps used on larger thread spools (cotton or covered polyester). Prevents spools from slipping off the spool pin and provides a smooth bearing surface for thread unwinding.
Smaller thread spool caps used on smaller spools of synthetic or specialty threads. Same function as large caps but sized for smaller spool diameters.

maintenance.action: Check needle eye for damage or burrs; replace if damaged. Verify upper thread tension is set correctly (3–4 on tension dial). Check thread path for snags or sharp edges. Ensure needle is inserted correctly with long groove facing front. Verify thread is compatible with needle size.

Inspect looper eye for wear or sharp edges; replace if damaged. Check looper thread tension. Verify looper timing is correct. Ensure looper thread passes freely through looper thread guide. Check that looper thread is wound correctly on spool.

maintenance.definition: Skipped stitches — needle failing to pick up looper thread
maintenance.action: Check needle timing: needle should be at its lowest point when looper tip is directly behind the needle. Inspect needle for bent or blunt tip; replace immediately if damaged. Verify needle is fully inserted and clamped securely. Check needle guard clearance — re-adjust if stitch length was changed. Verify needle gauge matches machine gauge setting.

maintenance.definition: Needle deflection / needle striking looper tip
maintenance.action: Immediately stop machine and replace bent needle. Check looper tip for damage; replace if cracked or worn. Re-check and re-set needle guard clearance using the gauge plate method. Verify needle guard bracket is not loose. Ensure correct needle gauge and type for material being sewn.

Reduce presser foot pressure using the adjusting screw. Check feed dog teeth for wear or damage; replace if teeth are dull. Verify stitch length is appropriate for material weight. Check that needle plate slots are not worn or burred. Ensure fabric is not being held too tightly ahead of the needle.

Reduce presser foot pressure. Reduce upper and lower thread tensions to minimum effective values. Increase stitch length. Check differential feed adjustment if available. For stretch fabrics, reduce thread tensions further and test on fabric sample before production.

Check the stitch length push button and ratchet mechanism for debris or damage. Clean ratchet teeth and re-engage eccentric wheel. Verify eccentric wheel lock screw is fully tightened. Check feed dog for damage or incorrect installation. Ensure fabric is feeding freely without resistance.

maintenance.definition: Presser foot not lifting via knee lifter
maintenance.action: Check knee lifter chain is connected and correctly tensioned. Inspect knee lifter lever return spring; replace if broken. Check presser bar lifter mechanism for binding or broken components. Verify presser bar moves freely when manually lifted. Lubricate pivot points if stiff.

maintenance.definition: Oil contamination on fabric / white staining
maintenance.action: This machine uses minimum lubrication; oil contamination indicates over-oiling. Wipe excess oil from machine. Check felt wicks are not saturated — only light dampening required. Verify wick holder SB7805001, wick 3×3 SB7806001, and wick 2×2 SB7811001 are correctly seated. Use only recommended oil: JXTG Nippon SEWINGLUBE N 10 (VG10) or equivalent Exxon Mobil Essotex SM10.

maintenance.definition: Chain looper tip broken or chipped
maintenance.action: Stop machine immediately upon tip break detection. Inspect needle guard for damage caused by tip contact. Check needle guard clearance setting. Replace broken looper (SB1506001 for L-looper). Set new needle guard using the standard gauge plate procedure after looper replacement. Verify timing before resuming production.

Check machine mounting cushions (Rubber Cushion H) for compression set or hardening; replace if deteriorated. Verify all mounting bolts are tight. Check pulley belt tension — belt should deflect 5–10 mm under firm thumb pressure. Inspect machine for loose panels or missing cover screws. Ensure machine is correctly seated on mounting table with correct spacers.

maintenance.definition: Lapper folder not feeding fabric correctly
maintenance.action: Check lapper guide plate is fully inserted and seated correctly. Inspect lapper folder for damage or distortion; replace if warped. Verify lapper guide plate washer is in place for correct clearance. Adjust fabric fold position by sliding the guide plate. Clean lint from lapper folder channel before re-threading.
